question: Vocal cord nodules (singer's nodules) characteristically occur at the junction of the anterior one-third and posterior two-thirds of the vocal cord — the point of maximum vibratory impact.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Vocal cord nodules form at the anterior one-third / posterior two-thirds junction due to maximum mucosal stress during vocal fold vibration. Knowing this site helps distinguish nodules from polyps and papillomas.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This is the high-stress zone during phonation. Nodules at this site are bilateral, symmetrical, and related to vocal abuse — distinguishing them from unilateral polyps which can occur anywhere on the cord.
